mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen monotonically from -13.3 to -9.7 over the last three weeks, indicating an established recovery momentum in shopping and leisure trips. This autocorrelated trend is expected to persist, pushing the next-4-week mean above the last-4-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved from -13.3 to -9.7 over three consecutive weeks
failure_condition: If the next four weekly RETAIL_REC means fail to exceed the current four-week mean, or reverse into a declining streak of two or more weeks, the momentum hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has fallen each week from 5.7 to 4.4, indicating households are spending less time confined at home. If RESIDENTIAL drops below 4.0, this signals a behavioral threshold where people reallocate freed time toward retail and recreation visits, lifting RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 4.0 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 5.7 to 4.4 over four weeks
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL crosses below 4.0 but RETAIL_REC does not rise in the subsequent two weeks, the threshold linkage is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: Joint improvement in TRANSIT (-34.3 to -31.7) and stability in WORKPLACES (around -9 to -8.3) jointly indicate restored commuting capacity that enables both work and incidental shopping trips. The interaction of rising transit use with stable workplace attendance should compound to raise RETAIL_REC over the next month more than either series alone would predict.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -34.3 to -31.7 while WORKPLACES stayed near -9 to -8.3
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both remain flat or improve but RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next four weeks, the interaction mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp PARKS rebound from -28.7 to -6.0 coincides with the Diwali festive period (mid-November), when outdoor and shopping activity typically spikes for celebrations. As the festival concludes, this seasonal surge is expected to taper, pulling RETAIL_REC down from its festive peak over the following weeks as post-festival normalization sets in.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose sharply from -28.7 to -6.0 in the week ending at decision point, consistent with Diwali-period activity
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC continues to rise for two or more weeks after the snapshot rather than reverting downward, the seasonal unwind hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Delhi experienced a rising COVID-19 case trajectory through November 2020; if TRANSIT mobility drops more than 5 points week-on-week from its current -31.7 level, this would signal renewed public caution or incipient restriction tightening, which would sharply curtail RETAIL_REC within the following week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 5 points week-on-week from -31.7
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT level stands at -31.7 at t-0w after a volatile four-week path
failure_condition: If TRANSIT drops more than 5 points in a week but RETAIL_REC does not decline in the subsequent week, the policy-tightening trigger is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has moved from -0.3 to 2.1, crossing into positive territory for the first time, reflecting growing consumer confidence in in-person errands. This rising baseline confidence is expected to spill over into broader retail and recreation visits over the coming month.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM turned positive at 2.1 in the most recent week after being near zero for three weeks
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM remains positive or rises further but RETAIL_REC's next-4-week mean does not exceed the prior 4-week mean, the spillover hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has been highly volatile, swinging from -19.0 to -28.7 to -14.1 to -6.0 across four weeks. If this volatility (week-on-week swing exceeding 10 points) continues, it signals unstable outdoor activity patterns that will translate into unstable, non-trending RETAIL_REC behavior rather than a clear directional move.
candidate_trigger: PARKS week-on-week change exceeds 10 points in absolute value
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS swung by more than 9 points in three of the last three weekly transitions
failure_condition: If PARKS volatility continues but RETAIL_REC instead shows a clear sustained rise over the next four weeks, the instability-transfer hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous combination of falling RESIDENTIAL (home time), rising WORKPLACES stability, and improving TRANSIT suggests coordinated policy easing. When all three move in the activity-supportive direction together, their combined effect should lift RETAIL_REC more strongly within one week than any single series would predict in isolation.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines, WORKPLACES stable or rising, and TRANSIT improving simultaneously in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell to 4.4, WORKPLACES held near -8.3, and TRANSIT improved to -31.7 in the same week
failure_condition: If all three supportive conditions co-occur in a week but RETAIL_REC does not rise in the following week, the coordinated-easing interaction hypothesis is rejected.
